title: The Vow of Bellbird Bay Again
premise: Juniper Nystrom built a career orchestrating perfect weddings for other people after her own engagement collapsed a decade ago, and she's sworn off love ever since. When Elias Ward — the stranger who wrote her anonymous letters of comfort for ten years, signed only 'B' — moves in next door to Bellbird Bay, she discovers the letters were never random: he was the boy who witnessed the accident that broke her family, carrying guilt he could never confess. As they grow close, Juniper must decide whether to expose the town patriarch whose cover-up ruined both their families, risking the wedding-planning empire that gave her everything, or protect her carefully rebuilt life and lose him. At the last ferry of the season, she chooses justice and Elias together, boarding with him as the bay closes for winter.
about_author: Quentin Iversen is the pen name of a former small-town journalist who spent years covering coastal communities before turning to romance. They write love stories about people who repair what the law and time could not.

chapters.title: The Last Wedding She Planned
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. She flawlessly executes a society wedding in Bellbird Bay while privately despising every vow she scripts, then retreats to her cottage to reread one of the ten annual letters from 'B' that have kept her afloat since her broken engagement. Beat: competence masking grief.

chapters.title: A Moving Truck at Number Nine
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. A quiet man named Elias Ward moves into the long-empty cottage next door; his dog destroys her hydrangeas and their first meeting is prickly, but something about his voice snags a memory she can't place. Beat: irritation laced with unearned familiarity.

chapters.title: Letters in Past Tense
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. He unpacks boxes containing drafts of every letter he ever sent Juniper, revealing to the reader that he has loved and watched over her from afar since the accident, and that moving here was a promise finally kept. Beat: tender secrecy and dread.

chapters.title: The Ferry Schedule
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. The autumn ferry season ends in six weeks, after which the bay is cut off until spring; her firm offers her a promotion in the city contingent on landing the Harrow wedding — the biggest contract of her career. Beat: ambition pulling against stillness.

chapters.title: Coffee, Storms, and Small Confessions
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. A storm knocks out power and Elias hosts Juniper and her found-family circle — retired ferry captain Mabel, teenage apprentice florist Dev — by candlelight; walls soften, but when Juniper mentions the letters, Elias goes pale. Beat: warmth with a hairline crack.

chapters.title: The Harrow Contract
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. She meets bride-to-be Celeste Harrow, daughter of town patriarch Aldous Harrow, and recognizes the family name from the accident report she's never been able to read twice. Taking the job means entering the house where everything ended. Beat: dread dressed as opportunity.

chapters.title: What B Never Wrote
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. Flashback chapter: sixteen-year-old Elias saw Aldous Harrow's truck force the Nystroms' car off the road and was paid and threatened into silence; the letters were penance. Now Juniper is planning a wedding inside the guilty house. Beat: guilt crystallizing into resolve.

chapters.title: Hydrangeas and Second Chances
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. Elias replants her destroyed flowers as an apology; they share an almost-kiss interrupted by Dev bursting in with news that the Harrow estate is demanding impossible changes. Beat: hope arriving exactly on schedule to be complicated.

chapters.title: The Tenth Letter
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. Rereading all ten letters, Juniper notices phrasing Elias used verbatim at dinner; she tests him with a quoted line and watches him flinch. She says nothing, but begins her own investigation into who 'B' really is. Beat: suspicion sharpening into obsession.

chapters.title: Celeste's Doubt
chapters.summary: Celeste's POV (guest). The bride confides in Juniper that she found her father's old insurance settlement papers and fears her family fortune was built on a lie; she asks Juniper, of all people, whether some truths should stay buried. Beat: dramatic irony tightening.

chapters.title: Mabel Knows Everything
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. Mabel reveals she ferried young Elias off the peninsula the night of the accident and has carried her own silence for a decade; she urges Juniper toward truth, not revenge. Beat: found family becoming the story's moral compass.

chapters.title: Almost
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Juniper and Elias finally kiss on the beach at low tide — then she confronts him with the letters, and he confesses everything except the name of who made him silent. Feeling managed rather than loved, she walks away. Beat: intimacy collapsing under withheld truth.

chapters.title: Planning a Wedding in a House of Lies
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. She returns to the Harrow estate professionally cold, using her access to search Aldous's study while Elias, watching from outside, realizes she knows more than he told her. Beat: love and investigation becoming indistinguishable.

chapters.title: Dev Runs Away
chapters.summary: Dev's POV (guest). Overwhelmed by the adults' secrets and his own fear of being sent back into foster care, Dev disappears; the whole bay searches, and Juniper finds him in the ferry shed, forcing her to admit she's been hiding too. Beat: found family tested and holding.

chapters.title: The Settlement Papers
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. With Celeste's help, Juniper obtains the settlement file proving Aldous paid off witnesses including a boy named E. Ward. Confronting Elias, she learns the full confession: he wasn't just silent, he took money meant for her family. Beat: betrayal inside forgiveness.

chapters.title: Aldous Harrow's Offer
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. Aldous privately offers Juniper the Harrow account, a city partnership, and hush money if she drops it; he reminds her the statute has run out and the law owes her nothing. Beat: the villain offering her exactly the life she thought she wanted.

chapters.title: What the Law Won't Do
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. Elias decides to confess publicly at the rehearsal dinner regardless of consequences, writing his final letter — this one unsigned no longer. Juniper must choose between stopping him to save her career or standing beside him. Beat: two people choosing courage separately.

chapters.title: The Rehearsal Dinner
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. In front of the assembled town, Elias tells the truth about the accident; Aldous detonates, Celeste calls off the wedding, and Juniper loses the contract that anchored her career — and stands up anyway, saying the letters saved her life. Beat: climax, public ruin and public love.

chapters.title: Aftermath in the Empty Marquee
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. Stripped of the Harrow account and facing professional fallout, Juniper sits among the abandoned wedding decorations; Mabel, Dev, and Celeste arrive not to console her but to plan something new. Beat: grief transmuting into reinvention.

chapters.title: The Bay Decides
chapters.summary: Multiple short POVs. The town reckons with the Harrows' fall; some shun Juniper and Elias, others bring casseroles and contracts; Celeste asks Juniper to plan her smaller, truer wedding in spring. Beat: justice rippling outward, community re-forming.

chapters.title: Last Ferry of the Season
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. On the final sailing day, Juniper must board for a city meeting that would rebuild everything she lost — or stay. She runs down the dock as the whistle blows, chooses Elias and the unfinished bay, and mails her resignation from the ferry itself. Beat: the choice the whole book promised.

chapters.title: The Vow of Bellbird Bay
chapters.summary: Epilogue, alternating POV. Spring: Celeste's honest little wedding on the beach, planned by Juniper's new independent studio with Dev as partner; Elias reads his eleventh letter aloud, this time signed with his name, and Juniper writes her own vow in reply. Beat: love in present tense at last.
